findings.title: Google Meet booking throws when destinationCalendar is missing
findings.body: EventManager.create now takes the first destinationCalendar and reads .integration with no null check. If the list is null, undefined, or [] (the value many callers now pass when nobody has a destination calendar), destructuring yields undefined and this throws TypeError before any video or calendar work. Previously optional chaining treated a missing calendar as not Google and replaced Meet with integrations:daily. Any Google Meet booking without a destination calendar, including confirmation and payment flows that pass [], now fails the whole create instead of falling back to Cal Video.

findings.title: Video references no longer store credentialId
findings.body: referencesToCreate used to persist result.credentialId for non-calendar results and now stores undefined whenever the result is not a calendar type. updateLocation in this same file still copies result.credentialId, so this is an accidental drop. handleCancelBooking only calls deleteMeeting when the video BookingReference has a credentialId, and there is no fallback lookup by integration type. New bookings will therefore not record the video credential, and cancelling them leaves the Zoom, Daily, or other video room in place.

findings.title: Secondary hosts are written to the first destination calendar
findings.body: createAllCalendarEvents loops each host destination and calls the provider with that host's credential, but it still passes the full destinationCalendar array. Only GoogleCalendarService picks the calendar by credentialId. Office 365 and Lark still use index 0, so a second host's token is aimed at the organizer's calendar id and the API call fails; that host never gets an event. CalDAV/Apple (BaseCalendarService) filters the host's calendars to the organizer's external id, matches nothing, and still returns success, so a booking reference is stored for an event that was never created. Google inserts also set the organizer attendee email from the first destination's externalId, so events written onto another host's calendar are attributed to the main calendar. Office 365 updateEvent and deleteEvent still always call /me/calendar/events/{id} and ignore the target calendar id, so a non-default Office event cannot be rescheduled or removed. Narrow the event to the destination currently being written before calling any provider.

findings.title: Google update/delete fallback can never select a calendar
findings.body: When externalCalendarId is missing, updateEvent and deleteEvent (same expression at line 317) search destinationCalendar for an entry whose externalId equals that missing value. That comparison is dead: if a calendar id had been passed, the first branch would already have used it. Previously the fallback was destinationCalendar.externalId. updateEvent then calls the Google API with calendarId undefined, so reschedule and location updates fail for any booking reference that has no externalCalendarId. deleteEvent falls through to primary, and a 404 is treated as success (line 335), so cancellation reports success while the event remains on the non-primary calendar.

findings.title: Collective host calendars are dropped from the event
findings.body: Other hosts' destination calendars are only appended with optional chaining. If neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, the field is null and the push is a no-op, so every other host is discarded. createAllCalendarEvents then falls back to credentials whose type is exactly "calendar", which never matches google_calendar, office365_calendar, and the rest, so nobody gets a calendar event. Separately, when the event type does have a destination calendar, that single calendar replaces the organizer's personal calendar, and only users.slice(1) are added, so the organizer's own calendar is never included. The stated goal that every collective host with a calendar app receives an event is not met in either case.

findings.title: Only the first destination calendar is stored on the booking
findings.body: Booking.destinationCalendar is a single relation and the create payload connects only evt.destinationCalendar[0]. The other hosts' calendars exist only on the in-memory event used for the immediate create. Stripe payment_intent.succeeded and setup_intent.succeeded, and PayPal handlePaymentSuccess, rebuild CalendarEvent from that one booking or user record and call EventManager.create. confirm.handler does the same and passes the evt to handleConfirmation. Collective bookings whose calendar events are created after payment or after organizer approval therefore only write the first calendar; every other host is skipped even if the initial assembly was correct.

findings.title: Cancelling a recurring series leaves other hosts' events
findings.body: The non-recurring branch deletes each calendar reference with that reference's credential. The all-remaining recurring branch was not updated: it still loads only the booking owner's calendar credentials and, for each instance, uses find() so only the first _calendar reference is deleted. It is also nested inside the new per-reference loop, so that incomplete deletion runs once per calendar reference. Other hosts' credentials are never loaded, Google 404s from the wrong token are treated as success, and the booking is already marked cancelled. After "cancel all remaining", secondary hosts keep the series on their calendars and stay busy.

findings.title: Organization slug condition is inverted
findings.body: This unrelated change flips slug assignment. Previously slug was set only when team billing was disabled, and requestedSlug only when billing was enabled. requestedSlug is still gated on IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED, but slug is now set in that same case and omitted otherwise. With billing off, new organizations are stored with neither slug nor requestedSlug, so the org subdomain cannot resolve. With billing on, the slug is published immediately and requestedSlug is also set, skipping the hold-for-billing gate.

findings.title: Google create falls back to primary instead of the chosen calendar
findings.body: createEvent selects the calendar only by matching destinationCalendar.credentialId to the credential used for the call. EventManager still has a legacy path for destination calendars with no credentialId, and that path calls createEvent without an external id. The find then misses, and the insert uses "primary" instead of the destination calendar's externalId, so the event is written to the wrong calendar and reported as success. The follow-up hangout-link patch at line 168 passes selectedCalendar with no primary fallback, so that patch runs with an undefined calendarId and the Meet link is never written into the description. The stored booking reference external id will not match the calendar that was actually written.

findings.title: Location updates store calendar references without ids
findings.body: updateLocation now sets externalCalendarId and credentialId from the EventResult. CalendarManager.updateEvent does not return either field (it also does not return externalId), and calendar updates populate updatedEvent rather than createdEvent. New booking references created by edit location therefore have an empty uid and no calendar credential or external calendar id. Previously those ids were copied from the destination calendar. The new multi-reference cancel path treats a missing credentialId as a legacy reference and calls deleteEvent on every calendar credential with a null external id, which no longer falls back to the real destination calendar.

findings.title: Seat-merge reschedule deletes only the first old calendar event
findings.body: updateAllCalendarEvents was changed to update every calendar reference, but the newBookingId merge path still does references.find() and deletes only the first _calendar reference. When a seated booking is moved onto an existing slot, every other host's old calendar event is left in place at the original time. Those hosts remain busy for a booking that has already been merged away.

findings.title: Webhook destinationCalendar shape is a breaking, inconsistent change
findings.body: destinationCalendar on CalendarEvent changed from a single object or null to an array or null, and that object is sent on booking webhooks. Consumers that read payload.destinationCalendar.externalId or .integration will now see an array (or crash). The PR is marked non-breaking, but this is a public payload change. Callers are also inconsistent: handleNewBooking sends null when there is no calendar, while confirm, payment webhooks, and cancel send []. The e2e suite only updated BOOKING_REJECTED to expect []; BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED still expect null, so the contract is not locked down.

findings.title: No test covers multi-host calendar create or cleanup
findings.body: The only test change is a webhook fixture expecting destinationCalendar: [] for BOOKING_REJECTED. Nothing books a collective event with two hosts on different calendar providers and asserts one successful write per host credential, and nothing asserts that cancel, reschedule, and payment-confirmation paths create or delete every stored booking reference. The checklist explicitly says no tests were added. The provider, recurring-cancel, and deferred-create bugs above would not be caught by CI.
